questions.solution:
Since, $\frac{7 x^2-5 x-18}{2 x^2+x-6} < 2\Rightarrow \frac{3 x^2-7 x-6}{(x+2)(2 x-3)} < 0 \Rightarrow \frac{(x-3)(3 x+2)}{(x+2)(2 x-3)} < 0$
So, $x \in \left(-2, \frac{-2}{3}\right) \cup \left(\frac{3}{2},$3\right).

questions.q: $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are the roots of the equation $x^3+3 x^2-10 x-24= 0. If \alpha(\beta+\gamma), \beta(\gamma+\alpha)$ and $\gamma(\alpha+\beta)$ are the roots of the equation $x^3+p x^2+q x+r=0$, then $q=$
questions.solution:
Since, $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ be the roots of the equation
$\begin{aligned}
& x^3+3 x^2-10 x-24=0 \\
& \because \alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\alpha \gamma=-10, \alpha \beta \gamma=24, \alpha+\beta+\gamma=-3
\end{aligned}$
Now, $(\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\alpha \gamma)^2=\alpha^2 \beta^2+\beta^2 \gamma^2+\alpha^2 \gamma^2\Rightarrow \alpha^2 \beta^2+\beta^2 \gamma^2+\alpha^2 \gamma^2=244 \quad+2 \alpha \beta \gamma(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Since, } q=\alpha \beta(\beta+\gamma)(\gamma+\alpha)+\beta \gamma(\gamma+\alpha)(\alpha+\beta) \\
& +\alpha \gamma(\beta+\gamma)(\alpha+\beta) \\
& =\alpha \beta \gamma(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+\alpha^2 \beta^2+\alpha \beta \gamma(\alpha+\beta+\gamma) \\
& +\beta^2 \gamma^2+\alpha \beta \gamma(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+\alpha^2 \gamma^2 \\
& =3 \cdot 24 \cdot(-3)+244=-216+244=28 .
\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & \qquad-1 < \frac{2 x^2+a x+2}{x^2+x+1} < 3 \\ & \text{ Consider }-1 < \frac{2 x^2+a x+2}{x^2+x+1} \Rightarrow 3 x^2+(a+1) x+3>0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{D} < 0 \Rightarrow(a+1)^2-36 < 0 \Rightarrow a^2+2 a-35 < 0\end{aligned}\Rightarrow(a+7)(a-5) < 0 \Rightarrow a \in(-7,5)$ ...(i)
$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Also, } \frac{2 x^2+a x+2}{x^2+x+1} < 3 \Rightarrow-x^2+(a-3) x-1 < 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{D} < 0 \Rightarrow(a-3)^2-4 < 0\end{aligned}\Rightarrow a^2-6 a+5 < 0 \Rightarrow(a-1)(a-5) < 0 \Rightarrow a \in(1,5)$ ...(ii)

$x^5-5 x^4+9 x^3-9 x^2+5 x-1=0$ ...(i) $\because a_0 x^{\mathrm{n}}+a_1 x^{\mathrm{n}-1}+a_2 x^{\mathrm{n}-2}+\ldots .+a_{\mathrm{n}-1} x+a_{\mathrm{n}}=0$
Here $a_0=-a_{\mathrm{n}}, a_1=-a_{\mathrm{n}-1}$ is class II reciprocal equation. So, eq (i) is an odd degree reciprocal equation By inspection $x=1$ is a root Using synthetic division $\begin{array}{c|cccccc}$1 & 1 & -5 & 9 & -9 & 5 & -1 \\& 0 & 1 & -4 & 5 & -4 & 1 \\\hline & 1 & -4 & 5 & -4 & 1 & 0\end{array} $x^4-4 x^3+5 x^2-4 x+1=0$ ...(ii) Equation (ii) is an even degree reciprocal equation of class I. $\frac{x^4-4 x^3+5 x^2-4 x+1}{x^2}=0 \Rightarrow\left(x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}\right)-4\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)+5=0$....(iii) Let $x+\frac{1}{x}=a$. So, Eq (iii) implies. $\begin{array}{ll} \left(a^2-2\right)-4 a+5=0 \Rightarrow(a-3)(a-1)=0 \\ \Rightarrow a=1 \text{ or } a=3 & a=3 \\ \Rightarrow a=1 & x+\frac{1}{x}=3 \\ \Rightarrow x+\frac{1}{x}=1 & \Rightarrow x^2-3 x+1=0 \\ \Rightarrow x^2-x+1=0 & x=\frac{3 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2} \end{array} \\ So, $\alpha_1=1, \alpha_2=$\frac{1+i \sqrt{3}}{2}, \alpha_$3=$\frac{1-i \sqrt{3}}{2}\begin{aligned}$& \alpha_4=$\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}, \alpha_$5=$\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}$\\ & $\frac{1}{\alpha_1^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_2^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_3^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_4^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_5^2}=$1+$\left(\frac{2}{1+i \sqrt{3}}\right)^$2+ \\ & \qquad$\left(\frac{2}{1-i \sqrt{3}}\right)^$2+$\left(\frac{2}{3+\sqrt{5}}\right)^$2+$\left(\frac{2}{3-\sqrt{5}}\right)^$2 \\ & =1+$\frac{(2-2 i \sqrt{3})^2}{16}+\frac{(2+2 i \sqrt{3})^2}{16}+\frac{(6-2 \sqrt{5})^2}{16}+\frac{(6+2 \sqrt{5})^2}{16}$\\ & =1+$\frac{4-12+4-12+36+20+36+20}{16}=$1+6=7 \end{aligned}

$\because \alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are roots of $x^3+a^2+b x+c=0\therefore \alpha+\beta+\gamma=-a \Rightarrow a=-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)\begin{aligned} & \alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha=b \\ & \alpha \beta \gamma=-c \Rightarrow c=-\alpha \beta \gamma\end{aligned}$
Let $\alpha^{\prime}, \beta^{\prime}$ and $\alpha^{\prime}$ are the roots of the equation
$\Rightarrow \alpha^{\prime}+\beta^{\prime}+\gamma^{\prime}=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2-2(\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha)\Rightarrow \alpha^{\prime}+\beta^{\prime}+\gamma^{\prime}=\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$...(i)
And $\alpha^{\prime} \beta^{\prime}+\beta^{\prime} \gamma^{\prime}+\gamma^{\prime} \alpha^{\prime}=b^2-2 a c\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \alpha^{\prime} \beta^{\prime}+\beta^{\prime} \gamma^{\prime}+\gamma^{\prime} \alpha^{\prime}=(\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha)^2-2(\alpha \beta \gamma) \alpha \beta \gamma \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha^{\prime} \beta^{\prime}+\beta^{\prime} \gamma^{\prime}+\gamma^{\prime} \alpha^{\prime}=(\alpha \beta)^2+(\beta \gamma)^2+\gamma^2 \alpha^2\end{aligned}=\alpha^2 \beta^2+\beta^2 \gamma^2+\gamma^2 \alpha^2$ ...(ii)
And $\alpha^{\prime} \beta^{\prime} \gamma^{\prime}=-\left(-c^2\right)=c^2=\alpha^2 \beta^2 \gamma^2$... (iii)
from eqs. (i), (ii) \& (iii) $\alpha^{\prime}=\alpha^2, \beta^{\prime}=\beta^2, \gamma^{\prime}=\gamma^2\therefore$ Roots are $\alpha^2, \beta^2$ and $\gamma^2$

Since, $2^{6 x}-3\left(2^{3 x+2}\right)+32=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow\left(2^{3 x}\right)^2-12\left(2^{3 x}\right)+32=0 \\ & \text{ Let } y=2^{3 x} \\ & \therefore y^2-12 y+32=0 \\ & (y-4)(y-8)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y=4 \quad \text{ or, } y=8 \\ & \Rightarrow 2^{3 x}=4 \quad \text{ or, } 2^{3 x}=8 \\ & \Rightarrow 2^{3 x}=22 \quad \text{ or, } 2^{3 x}=23\end{aligned}\Rightarrow x=\frac{2}{3} \quad$ or, $x=1$

questions.solution:
Since, $\alpha_1, \alpha_2 \ \text{$ and $} \alpha_3$ are the roots of $x^3+3 x+2=0$.
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3=0 \\ & \alpha_1 \alpha_2+\alpha_2 \alpha_3+\alpha_3 \alpha_1=3 \\ & \alpha_1 \alpha_2 \alpha_3=-2\end{aligned}$
Now, $\alpha_1^5+\alpha_2^5+\alpha_3^5=\alpha_1^3 \cdot \alpha_1^2+\alpha_2^3 \alpha_2^2+\alpha_3^3 \alpha_3^2\begin{aligned} & =\left(-3 \alpha_1-2\right) \cdot \alpha_1^2+\left(-3 \alpha_2-2\right) \alpha_2^2+\left(-3 \alpha_3-2\right) \alpha_3^2 \\ & =-3 \alpha_1^3-2 \alpha_1^2-3 \alpha_2^3-2 \alpha_2^2-3 \alpha_3^3-2 \alpha_3^2 \\ & =-\left(-3 \alpha_1-2\right)-3\left(3 \alpha_2-2\right)-3\left(3 \alpha_3-2\right)-2\left(\alpha_1^2+\alpha_2^2+\alpha_3^2\right) \\ & =9\left(\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3\right)-2\left[\left(\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3\right)^2-2\left(\alpha_2 \alpha_1+\alpha_2 \alpha_3\right.\right. \\ & =9 \times 0-2\left[0^2-2 \times(3)\right]+18 \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha_1^5+\alpha_2^5+\alpha_3^5=30\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}
& \alpha+\beta+\gamma=a \\

& \Rightarrow(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2-\alpha \beta-\beta \gamma-\gamma \alpha\right)+3 \alpha \beta \gamma=0 \\
& \Rightarrow a\left((\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2-3(\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha)\right)+3 c=0 \\
& \Rightarrow a\left[a^2-3 b\right]+3 c=0 \\
& \Rightarrow a^3-3 a b+3 c=0 \Rightarrow a^3+3 c=3 a b

questions.solution:
Given, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $2 x^2+6 x+k=0\Rightarrow \alpha+\beta=-\frac{6}{2}=-3$ and $\alpha \beta=\frac{k}{2}$
Now, $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}+\frac{\beta}{\alpha}=\frac{\alpha^2+\beta^2}{\alpha \beta}=\frac{(\alpha+\beta)^2-2 \alpha \beta}{\alpha \beta}\Rightarrow \frac{\alpha}{\beta}+\frac{\beta}{\alpha}=\frac{2(9-k)}{k}=\frac{18}{k}-2\because \quad k \lt  0\left(\frac{18}{k}-2\right) \lt  0, \forall k \lt  0$
Thus, $\left[\frac{\alpha}{\beta}+\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\right]_{\max }=\left[\frac{18}{k}-2\right]=\left[\frac{18}{k}\right]-2=-2$

questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{x^2+1}{x^4+4}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2-2 x+2}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2+2 x+2} \\ & \Rightarrow 3 A+2 B+3 C=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
$\frac{x^2+1}{x^4+4}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2-2 x+2}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2+2 x+2}\Rightarrow \frac{x^2+1}{x^4+4}=\frac{(A x+B)\left(x^2+2 x+2\right)+(C x+D)\left(x^2-2 x+2\right)}{\left(x^2+2\right)^2-(2 x)^2}\Rightarrow x^2+1=(A+C) x^3+(2 A+B-2 C+D) x^2+(2 A+2 B+2 C-2 D) x+(2 B+2 D)$On comparing both sides,
A+C=0 \Rightarrow A=-C, 2 B+2 D=1 and $2 A+B-2 C+D=1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad 2(A-C)+B+D=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 4 A+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 4 A=1-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad A=\frac{1}{8} \text{ and } C=-\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}$
Now, $2 A+2 B+2 C-2 D=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad 2(A+C)+2(B-D)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad B=D \\ & \text{$ and $} 2 B+2 D=1\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad 4 B=1 \Rightarrow B=D=\frac{1}{4}$
Now, $3 A+2 B+3 C=2 B \quad[\because 3 A+3 C=0]=2 D$

questions.q: The sum of all the real roots of the equation $\left|x - 2\right|2 + \left|x - 2\right| - 2 = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Given:

$\left|x - 2\right|2 + \left|x - 2\right| - 2 = 0 . . . . \left(1\right)

Putting $y = $\left|x - 2\right|$, then we can rewrite $\left(1\right)$ as

$y^{2} + y - 2 = 0$

$⇒ y^{2} + 2y - y - 2 = 0$

$⇒ y\left(y + 2\right) - \left(y + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(y - 1\right)\left(y + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ y = 1, - 2$

Since, $y ≥ 0$, so

$y = \left|x - 2\right| = 1$

$⇒ x - 2 = \pm1$

$⇒ x = 3or1$

Required sum is $= 3 + 1 = 4$

questions.q: Difference between the corresponding roots of $x^{2} + ax + b = 0 \text{ and } x^{2} + bx + a = 0$ is same and $a \ne b, ⁡$then
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha, \beta & \gamma, \delta$ are the roots of the equations $x^{2} + a x + b = 0 and x^{2} + bx + a = 0$ respectively.

Therefore,

$\alpha + \beta = - a$

$\alpha\beta = b$

Also, for the second equation

$\gamma + \delta = - b$

$\gamma\delta = a$

Given that,

$\alpha - \beta = \gamma - \delta$

$⇒ \left(\alpha - \beta\right)^{2}$ = $\left(\gamma - \delta\right)^{2}

$⇒ $\left(\alpha + \beta\right)^{2}$ - 4\alpha\beta = $\left(\gamma + \delta\right)^{2}$ - 4\gamma\delta$

$⇒ a^{2} - 4b = b^{2} - 4a$

$⇒ $\left(a^{2} - b^{2}\right)$ + 4 $\left(a - b\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ $\left(a - b\right)\left(a + b\right)$ + 4 $\left(a - b\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ $\left(a - b\right)\left(4 + a + b\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ a + b + 4 = 0$

\left[∵ a \ne b\right]

$

questions.q: For what values of $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, the quadratic expression $\left(x + a\right)   \left(x + 1991\right)+ 1$ can be factorised as $\left(x + b\right)\left(x + c\right), where $b, c \in $\mathbb{Z}$?
questions.solution:
Since, he quadratic expression $\left(x + a\right) \left(x + 1991\right) + 1$ can be factorised as $\left(x + b\$ \right) $\left( x + c\right)$, therefore

$\left(x + a\right) \left(x + 1991\right) + 1 = \left( x + b\\right) \left( x + c\right)

This implies that \left(x + a\right) \left(x + 1991\right) + 1$ has roots& $- b & - c$ i.e., integer roots. So, discriminant of $x^{2} + \left(1991 + a\right)x + 1991a + 1 = 0$must be perfect square.

$\left(1991 + a\right)$2 - 4 $\left(1991a + 1\right)$ = m^{2}$

$⇒ $\left(1991 - a\right)$2 = m^{2} + 4$

$⇒ $\left(1991 - a\right)$2 - m^{2} = 4$

$⇒ $\left(1991 - a - m\right) \left(1991 - a + m\right) = 4$

Since, both $\left(1991 - a - m\right)$ and $\left(1991 - a + m\right) are integers, therefore possible choices are

\left(1991 - a - m\right) \left(1991 - a + m\right) = 1 \times4$

$\left(1991 - a - m\right) \left(1991 - a + m\right)$ = - 1 \times $\left(- 4\right)$

$\left(1991 - a - m\right) \left(1991 - a + m\right)$ = 2 \times2$

\left(1991 - a - m\right) \left(1991 - a + m\right) = - 2 \times \left(-2\right)

Only possible result is $m = 0$, so

$a = 1989, 1993$

questions.q: $2 + \sqrt{5}, 1$& are roots of the cubic equation given by
questions.solution:
We know that, in a cubic& equation with rational coefficients has a& irrational& root $\alpha + \sqrt{\beta}$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are rational and $\beta$ is not a perfect square, then it has also a conjugate root $\alpha - \sqrt{\beta}$.

Hence, $1, 2 + \sqrt{5}, 2 - \sqrt{5}$ are the roots of cubic equation.

We know that, if $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are& the roots of& cubic equation, then its equation is $x^{3} - \left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)$ x^{2} + $\left(\alpha\beta + \alpha\gamma + \beta\gamma\right)$ x - $\left(\alpha\beta\gamma\right).

Let, \alpha =1, \beta =2 + \sqrt{5}, \gamma =2 - \sqrt{5}$

\alpha + \beta + \gamma =1 + 2 + \sqrt{5} +$2 - \sqrt{5} =5$, $\alpha\beta + \alpha\gamma + \beta\gamma = ==1\left(2 + \sqrt{5}\right) + \left(2 + \sqrt{5}\right)\left(2 - \sqrt{5}\right) ++1\left(2 - \sqrt{5}\right) =2 + \sqrt{5} +4 - 5 + 2 - \sqrt{5} =3$

$\alpha\beta\gamma ==1\left(2 + \sqrt{5}\right)\left(2 - \sqrt{5}\right) = -1$.

Hence, required cubic equation is $x^{3} - 5x^{2} + 3x + 1 = 0$.

$\dfrac{3x - 2}{( x + 1{)}^{2} ( x + 3 )} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{( x + 1{)}^{2}} + \dfrac{C}{x + 3}$

questions.q: The sum of the roots of the equation $e^{4t} - 10e^{3t} + 29e^{2t} - 22e^{t} + 4 = 0$& is
questions.solution:
Let& $x = e^{t} ⇒ t = \log_{\mathrm{e}}x$

Then, the given equation reduces to $x^{4} - 10x^{3} + 29x^{2} - 22x + 4 = 0$

Now, product of roots taken all at a time of a biquadratic equation is $\dfrac{constantterm}{coefficientofx^{2}}$.

Let ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, {x}_{3}$ and& ${x}_{4}$ are the four roots of& $x^{4} - 10x^{3} + 29x^{2} - 22x + 4 = 0$, then ${x}_{1}{x}_{2}{x}_{3}{x}_{4} = \dfrac{4}{1} = 4$.

Taking $log$ both sides, we get& $\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left({x}_{1}{x}_{2}{x}_{3}{x}_{4}\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}4$

$⇒ \log_{\mathrm{e}}{x}_{1} + \log_{\mathrm{e}}{x}_{2} + \log_{\mathrm{e}}{x}_{3} + \log_{\mathrm{e}}{x}_{4} = 2\log_{\mathrm{e}}2$

$⇒ {t}_{1} + {t}_{2} + {t}_{3} + {t}_{4} = 2\log_{\mathrm{e}}2$

Where ${t}_{1}, {t}_{2}, {t}_{3}$ and& ${t}_{4}$ are the roots of the equation& $e^{4t} - 10e^{3t} + 29e^{2t} - 22e^{t} + 4 = 0$.

Hence, sum of roots is $2\log_{\mathrm{e}}2$.

questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ If } \frac{x^3}{(2 x-1)(x-1)^2}=A+\frac{B}{2 x-1}+\frac{C}{x-1} \\ & +\frac{D}{(x-1)^2}, \text{ then } 2 A-3 B+4 C+5 D=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
We have, $\frac{x^3}{(2 x-1)(x-1)^2}=\frac{x^3}{2 x^3-5 x^2+4 x-1}$
Now, consider $$ \begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{5 x^2-4 x+1}{2 x^3-5 x^2+4 x-1}\right) \\ & \quad=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{B}{2 x-1}+\frac{C}{x-1}+\frac{D}{(x-1)^2}\right) \\ & \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{5 x^2-4 x+1}{2 x^3-5 x^2+4 x-1}\right) \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{B(x-1)^2+C(x-1)(2 x-1)+D(2 x-1)}{(2 x-1)(x-1)^2}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 5 x^2-4 x+1 \\ & \quad=B(x-1)^2+C(x-1)(2 x-1)+D(2 x-1) \end{aligned} $$ Put $x=1$, we get $$ D=2 $$ Put $x=1 / 2$, we get $B=+1$ Now put $x=0$, we get $$ \begin{aligned} 1 & =B+C-D \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1 & =+1+C-2 \quad \Rightarrow \quad C=2 \end{aligned} $$ Now, $\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{5 x^2-4 x+1}{(2 x-1)(x-1)^2}\right)$ $$ \begin{gathered} =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{+1}{2 x-1}+\frac{2}{x-1}+\frac{2}{(x-1)^2}\right) \\ =\frac{+\frac{1}{2}}{2 x-1}+\frac{\frac{2}{2}}{x-1}+\frac{1}{(x-1)^2} \end{gathered} $$ Put in Eq. (i), we get $$ =\frac{1}{2}+\left(\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{2 x-1}+\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{1}{(x-1)^2}\right) $$ By comparing $A=1 / 2, B=1 / 2, C=1, D=1$. Now, $$ \begin{aligned} & 2 A-3 B+4 C+5 D \\ & =2 \times \frac{1}{2}-3 \times \frac{1}{2}+4 \times 1+5 \times 1 \\ & =1-\frac{3}{2}+4+5=10-\frac{3}{2}=\frac{17}{2} \end{aligned} $$

questions.q: If $x$ is real, then the minimum value of $y=\frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+x+1}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $y=\frac{1-x+x^2}{1+x+x^2}$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get $\begin{aligned}\frac{d y}{d x}& =\frac{\left(1+x+x^2\right)(-1+2 x)-\left(1-x+x^2\right)(1+2 x)}{\left(1+x+x^2\right)^2}\\
& =\frac{-1+2 x-x+2 x^2-x^2+2 x^3-1-2 x+x}{\left(1+x+x^2\right)^2}\\
& =\frac{-2+2 x^2-x^2-2 x^3}{\left(1+x+x^2\right)^2}\\
& =\frac{2 x^2-2}{\left(1+x+x^2\right)^2}
\end{aligned} =\frac{2\left(x^2-1\right)}{\left(1+x+x^2\right)^2}$ Put $\frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow x^2=1 \Rightarrow x= \pm 1$
Now, $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\frac{\left.\left(1+x+x^2\right)(1+2 x)\right]}{\left(1+x+x^2\right)^4} \begin{aligned}& =\frac{4\left(1+x+x^2\right)\left[\left(1+x+x^2\right) x-\left(x^2-1\right)(1+2 x)\right]}{\left(1+x+x^2\right)^4}\\
& =\frac{4\left[x+x^2+x^3-x^2-2 x^3+1+2 x\right]}{\left(1+x+x^2\right)^3}\\
& =\frac{4\left(1+3 x-x^3\right)}{\left(1+x+x^2\right)^3}
\end{aligned}$ At $x=1$, $\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)_{x=1}& =\frac{4\left[1+3(1)-1^3\right]}{\left(1+1+1^2\right)^3}\\
& =\frac{4(3)}{3^3}=\frac{4}{9}>0
\end{aligned} At $ x=-1$, \begin{aligned}& \left(\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)_{x=-1}=\frac{4\left[1+3(-1)-(-1)^3\right]}{\left[1+(-1)+(-1)^2\right]^3}\\
& =\frac{4(1-3+1)}{(1-1+1)^3}=4(-1)=-4 < 0
\end{aligned} $\therefore$ By second derivative test, $f$ is minimum at $x=1 and $the minimum value is given by y=\frac{1-1+1}{1+1+1}=\frac{1}{3}$

Given, $\quad a=\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$...(i) $b=\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha$...(ii) $c=(\alpha+\beta)(\beta+\gamma)(\gamma+\alpha)$...(iii) In cubic equation the sum of the roots $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-\left(\frac{-6}{1}\right)=6\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha=\left(\frac{11}{1}\right)=11$ product of the roots $\alpha \cdot \beta \cdot \gamma=-\left(\frac{-6}{1}\right)=6$ From Eq. Let $\alpha=1, \beta=2, \gamma=3$ Now, $\quad a=\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=1+4+9=14b=\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha=2+6+3=11c=(\alpha+\beta)(\beta+\gamma)(\gamma+\alpha)=3 \cdot 5 \cdot 4=60$ From the values of $a, b$ and $c$ it is clear that $b < a < c$.

If $m_1$ and $m_2$ are the roots of the equation
$x^2+(\sqrt{3}+2) x+(\sqrt{3}-1)=0,$
then the area of the triangle formed by the lines $y=m_1 x, y=m_2 x$ and $y=c$
questions.solution:
Since, $m_1$ and $m_2$ are the roots of the equation $x^2+(\sqrt{3}+2) x+(\sqrt{3}-1)=0$
then $\quad m_1+m_2=-(\sqrt{3}+2)$,
$m_1 m_2=\sqrt{3}-1$
$\therefore m_1-m_2=\sqrt{\left(m_1+m_2\right)^2-4 m_1 m_2}$
$=\sqrt{(3+4+4 \sqrt{3}-4 \sqrt{3}+4)}$
$=\sqrt{11}$
and coordinates of the vertices of the given triangles are $(0,0),\left(c / m_1, c\right)$ and $\left(c / m_2, c\right)$. Hence, the required area of triangle
$=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}0 & 0 & 1 \\ \frac{c}{m_1} & c & 1 \\ \frac{c}{m_2} & c & 1\end{array}\right|=\frac{1}{2} c^2\left|\left(\frac{1}{m_1}-\frac{1}{m_2}\right)\right|$
$=\frac{1}{2} c^2 \frac{\left|m_2-m_1\right|}{m_1 m_2}$
$=\frac{1}{2} c^2 \frac{\sqrt{11}}{(\sqrt{3}-1)}$
$=\frac{1}{2} c^2 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{11} \cdot(\sqrt{3}+1)}{(\sqrt{3}-1)(\sqrt{3}+1)}$
$=\left(\frac{\sqrt{33}+\sqrt{11}}{4}\right) \cdot c^2$

questions.solution:
$\frac{3 x^2+x+1}{(x-1)^4}=\frac{a}{(x-1)}+\frac{b}{(x-1)^2}+\frac{c}{(x-1)^3}+\frac{d}{(x-1)^4}3 x^2+x+1=a(x-1)^3+b(x-1)^2+c(x-1)+d3 x^2+x+1=a\left(x^3-1+3 x-3 x^2\right)+b\left(x^2+1-2 x\right)+c(x-1)+d3 x^2+x+1=a x^3+(-3 a+b) x^2+(3 a-2 b+c) x+(-a+b-c+d)$
On comparing the coefficient of like powers of $x$ on both sides.
$a=0,-3 a+b=3,3 a-2 b+c=2\Rightarrow \quad b=3 \Rightarrow 0-6+c=1\Rightarrow \quad c=7$
and $\quad-a+b-c+d=1\Rightarrow \quad 0+3-7+d=1\Rightarrow \quad d=5$
Hence, $\quad\left[\begin{array}{ll}a & b \\ c & d\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{ll}0 & 3 \\ 7 & 5\end{array}\right]$

Required equation whose roots are $\sin ^2 18^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $\cos ^2 36^{{}^{\circ}}$, is

On squaring both sides of equation (i)

\Rightarrow & 1+2\left(\frac{c}{a}\right) & =\frac{b^2}{a^2} \\
\Rightarrow & 2 \cdot \frac{c}{a} & =\frac{b^2-a^2}{a^2} \\
\Rightarrow & -a^2+b^2 & =2 a c \\
\therefore & E_2: b^2-a^2 & =2 a c \text{ is true }
\end{array}$\Rightarrow E_1$ and $E_2$ both are true.$

\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$, are the roots of the equation $x^3+4 x+1=0$, then $(\alpha+\beta)^{-1}+(\beta+\gamma)^{-1}+(\gamma+\alpha)^{-1}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Since, $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are the roots of the equation $x^3+4 x+1=0\therefore \quad \alpha+\beta+\gamma=0\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha=4$

questions.q: Let $a \neq 0$ and $p(x)$ be a polynomial of degree greater than 2. If $p(x)$ leaves remainders a and $-a$ when divided respectively by $x+a$ and $x-a$, then the remainder when $p(x)$ is divided by $x^2-a^2$ is :
questions.solution:
Let the remainder be $R(x)$, then
$R(x)=P(x)+q$
Given, $\quad R(-a)=a \Rightarrow-P a+q=a\ldots$ (i)
and $R(a)=-a \Rightarrow P a+q=-a\ldots$ (ii)
On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$P=1, q=0\therefore \quad R(x)=-x$

questions.q: If the equations $x^2+a x+b=0$ and $x^2+b x+a=0(a \neq b)$ have a common root, then $a+b$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha$ be the common root, then $\begin{array}{rlrl}& \alpha^2+a \alpha+ b & =0 \\
\text{ and }& \alpha^2+b \alpha+ a & =0 \\
\therefore & & \frac{\alpha^2}{a^2-b^2}& =\frac{\alpha}{b-a}=\frac{1}{b-a}\\
\Rightarrow & & \frac{\alpha}{b-a}& =\frac{1}{b-a} \Rightarrow \alpha=1 \\
\text{ Now, } \quad& \frac{\alpha^2}{a^2-b^2}& =\frac{\alpha}{b-a}\\
\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{(a+b)(a-b)}& =\frac{1}{-(a-b)}\\
\Rightarrow & a+b & =-1
\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The biquadratic equation, two of whose roots are $1+i, 1-\sqrt{2}$, is
questions.solution:
When $1+i, 1-i$ are the roots, then
Sum of the roots $=1+i+1-i=2$
and product of the roots $=1+1=2$
The equation is $x^2-2 x+2=0$
When $1-\sqrt{2}, 1+\sqrt{2}$ are the roots, then
Sum of the roots $=1-\sqrt{2}+1+\sqrt{2}=2$
Product of the roots $=1-2=-1$
The equation is $x^2-2 x-1=0$
The bi-quadratic equation is
$\begin{array}{r}\left(x^2-2 x+2\right)\left(x^2-2 x-1\right)=0 \\ \left(x^4-(2+2) x^3=(-1+4+2) x^2\right.\\ =(2-4) x-2=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad x^4-4 x^3+5 x^2-2 x-2=0\end{array}$
